04ff5c81-d090-4543-aeb5-2640af323fc1.heading_path: Materials and methods > Ethics approval and informed consent
04ff5c81-d090-4543-aeb5-2640af323fc1.text: The parent REasons for Geographic and Racial Disparities in Stroke (REGARDS) study and this ancillary study were approved by the Institutional Review Board of the University of Alabama at Birmingham. The parent REGARDS study obtained written consent from all cohort participants, including permission for review of medical records. The IRB waived requirement for informed consent for this ancillary study. The identities of the study participants were confidential and not accessible to the investigators.

5a265275-3a46-49dd-a8e1-15ffa939914e.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
5a265275-3a46-49dd-a8e1-15ffa939914e.heading_path: Materials and methods > Study design and data collection – The REGARDS cohort
5a265275-3a46-49dd-a8e1-15ffa939914e.text:
REGARDS is a longitudinal, population-based cohort including 30,239 community-living adults aged ≥45 years from across the continental US. Enrollment occurred between January 2003 and October 2007, and included a baseline interview where participants answered questions about demographics, health behaviors, diagnosed medical conditions and medication usage. As a part of an in-home visit, trained personnel collected vital sign measurements and obtained blood and urine samples from participants [ 12 ]. REGARDS conducted follow-up contacts with each participant at 6-month intervals for up to 19 years, identifying interim health and hospitalization events.

For this ancillary study, trained research personnel conducted structured chart reviews of hospitalizations for CABG surgery. Medical records included Emergency Department and admission notes, surgical notes, discharge summaries, and clinical laboratory values. Abstracted information pertinent to this study included history of maintenance dialysis, kidney transplant, use of dialysis during hospitalization and all creatinine values throughout the admission [ 13 , 14 ]. Research personnel had access to identifiable medical record information. The research team reviewed medical records during the period October 1, 2022 to May 1, 2024.

62f0100f-d414-42eb-a68f-e516743f5563.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
62f0100f-d414-42eb-a68f-e516743f5563.heading_path: Materials and methods > Outcomes – Identification of Post-CABG surgery acute kidney injury
62f0100f-d414-42eb-a68f-e516743f5563.text:
For the present study, we included participants who experienced hospitalizations associated with CABG surgery after their REGARDS baseline visit. The parent REGARDS study identified all hospitalizations and obtained copies of medical records for suspected coronary heart disease (CHD) events, which included CABG surgeries [ 12 , 15 ]. For participants who had multiple CABG surgery procedures during study follow-up, we selected the first surgery. We excluded participants who experienced a myocardial infarction or acute heart failure exacerbation during the CABG-associated hospitalization. Due to limitations in the available records, we were not able to obtain information on perioperative characteristics such as CABG procedure, bypass time, contrast exposure or medications.

The primary outcome of the study was the development of AKI in the post-operative period. We defined the participant’s baseline creatinine as the lowest serum creatinine value in the 48 hours prior to CABG surgery and the post-CABG surgery creatinine as the highest creatinine value following CABG surgery. To define AKI presence and severity, we used the Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria, defined as a minimum rise in serum creatinine (SCr) of ≥0.3 mg/dL between the highest and baseline creatinine values [ 16 ].

ad60b45a-bb64-4be2-b8a1-45ed69f81c05.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
ad60b45a-bb64-4be2-b8a1-45ed69f81c05.heading_path: Materials and methods > Exposures – Biomarkers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury
ad60b45a-bb64-4be2-b8a1-45ed69f81c05.text: The primary exposures were urine biomarkers of kidney tubule dysfunction (A1M, UMOD, EGF) and injury (KIM-1). These markers were based upon urine samples obtained near the time of participant enrollment in the parent REGARDS study. Blood and urine samples obtained during the initial in-home visit were centrifuged within 2 hours of collection, placed on ice and shipped overnight to the University of Vermont. Upon arrival, laboratory researchers centrifuged the samples at 30,000 g and 4 °C.

1372a563-9cb8-4527-94f3-3fa8e698a42a.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
1372a563-9cb8-4527-94f3-3fa8e698a42a.text: Covariates included demographics (age, sex, race), urine creatinine (to account for urine tonicity at time of collection), body mass index (BMI), chronic medical conditions (hypertension and diabetes mellitus) and baseline glomerular kidney measures (eGFR and urine albumin) all measured at the REGARDS baseline visit. These covariates were selected for their biologic plausibility. We identified each chronic medical condition either through the participant’s self-report or their use of disease-specific medications. Additionally, we included a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus if the participant had baseline laboratory values of either a fasting blood glucose of >126 mg/dL or a non-fasting blood glucose of >200 mg/dL. We calculated baseline eGFR using the participant’s baseline serum creatinine and serum cystatin C measurements according to the 2021 CKD-EPI equation without race [ 17 ].

708e5884-eead-4920-878f-0f47ec458894.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
708e5884-eead-4920-878f-0f47ec458894.text: We reported continuous variables using means and standard deviations or medians with quartiles, as appropriate. We examined the inter-relations between biomarkers using Spearman coefficients. We performed unconditional logistic regression (univariable and multivariable) to estimate the association between each biomarker (log 2 transformed and quartiles) with odds of AKI. The log 2 transformation accounts for data skew, allows interpretation as “per 2-fold higher”, and facilitates comparison of strengths of associations with our prior work. We examined sequential multivariable models. Model 1 adjusted for age, sex, race, time from REGARDS interview to CABG surgery, and urine creatinine. Model 2 included Model 1 and history of diabetes, hypertension, and BMI at REGARDS enrollment. Finally, Model 3 included Model 2 variables and eGFR and urine albumin at enrollment. We also tested the associations between each biomarker and post-CABG surgery AKI stratified by time from REGARDS interview to CABG surgery hospitalization. Statistical significance was set at 0.05 (two-tailed), and we calculated 95% confidence intervals for all odds ratios. We performed all analyses using SAS version 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA).

c0dbb457-e4aa-4c0e-829f-748dbc16760a.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
c0dbb457-e4aa-4c0e-829f-748dbc16760a.text:
Among the 30,239 REGARDS participants, 760 (2.5%) underwent CABG surgery [ 17 ]. We excluded 366 participants with illegible or incomplete records, 3 participants for a history of hemodialysis use or kidney transplant at hospital admission, 15 participants for missing serum creatinine values and 2 participants who underwent a cardiac procedure other than CABG, resulting in a final analytic sample of 394 individuals ( Fig 1 ).

Of the 394 participants, 176 (45%) experienced AKI after their CABG surgery. Individuals who were male or Black were more likely to experience AKI. The AKI group had slightly lower eGFR values and higher urine ACR values at REGARDS baseline compared to the non-AKI group ( Table 1 ).

The kidney tubule markers showed weak to moderate correlation (Spearman correlation coefficient −0.12 to 0.50). ( Table 2 ) The highest correlation (0.50) was between KIM-1 and EGF. Higher A1M was inversely correlated with eGFR. EGF and UMOD were directly correlated with eGFR, but the correlations were weak. Higher A1M was directly correlated with albuminuria, whereas EGFR and urine UMOD were inversely correlated with albuminuria.

5cf91107-cb79-45b3-966d-91ff8c67a177.text: Our study builds upon our prior research from the SPRINT blood pressure trial, where we found that biomarkers of kidney tubular dysfunction (A1M, UMOD, EGF), but not injury, were associated with future development of AKI in a subgroup of CKD patients [ 6 , 18 – 21 ]. The current study suggests that markers of tubule dysfunction measured among community-based adults at a stable phase of health, may be associated with higher odds of AKI after future CABG surgery. b98b71cc-f189-4598-b28f-779a1f772bb4.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
b98b71cc-f189-4598-b28f-779a1f772bb4.text:
Our study builds upon our prior research from the SPRINT blood pressure trial, where we found that biomarkers of kidney tubular dysfunction (A1M, UMOD, EGF), but not injury, were associated with future development of AKI in a subgroup of CKD patients [ 6 , 18 – 21 ]. The current study suggests that markers of tubule dysfunction measured among community-based adults at a stable phase of health, may be associated with higher odds of AKI after future CABG surgery. These associations were independent of risk factors and glomerular kidney markers used routinely in clinical practice (eGFR and albuminuria).

Prior studies largely focused on changes in KIM-1 in the perioperative period as a measure of dynamic tubular injury from the surgical procedure. This is different from the current study in which urine KIM-1 was measured in community-based individuals at a time of relative health, during which KIM-1’s signal as a sensitive marker of acute tubular injury may have been limited. This observation is similar to other studies showing weak or absent associations of KIM-1 with outcomes such as rapid kidney function decline or incident hypertension in ambulatory populations in which it was measured during their healthy baseline [ 24 ]. Collectively, we infer from these data that KIM-1 may be most useful as a biomarker of acute tubular injury as opposed to a long-term marker of tubular injury.

Prior studies largely focused on changes in KIM-1 in the perioperative period as a measure of dynamic tubular injury from the surgical procedure. This is different from the current study in which urine KIM-1 was measured in community-based individuals at a time of relative health, during which KIM-1’s signal as a sensitive marker of acute tubular injury may have been limited. This observation is similar to other studies showing weak or absent associations of KIM-1 with outcomes such as rapid kidney function decline or incident hypertension in ambulatory populations in which it was measured during their healthy baseline [ 24 ]. Collectively, we infer from these data that KIM-1 may be most useful as a biomarker of acute tubular injury as opposed to a long-term marker of tubular injury.

e7b7ec03-1930-40d8-a194-6e0650f175c0.paper_title: Markers of kidney tubule dysfunction and injury and long-term risk of acute kidney injury following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
e7b7ec03-1930-40d8-a194-6e0650f175c0.text: Biomarkers of tubule health, measured in community-based adults at a stable phase of health, are associated with AKI events after future CABG surgery. This finding was stronger for markers of kidney tubule dysfunction than for markers of tubule injury. Higher A1M and lower urine UMOD were associated with higher odds of AKI, independent of eGFR, albuminuria, and AKI risk factors. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms of AKI after bypass surgery and provide opportunities to identify higher risk patients for post-CABG surgery AKI where preventive strategies may be warranted.

Alpha-thalassemia is particularly prevalent in the Mediterranean, sub-Saharan Africa, and parts of Asia, although the disease is now prevalent in many regions of Europe and America due to recent migrations ( 13 ). Saudi Arabia has a high prevalence rate of alpha-thalassemia that varies according to the geographic location. Mecca and the eastern regions have a higher prevalence of 6% than other parts of the country, such as the northern regions, which have a prevalence of 0.4% ( 14–17 ).

Recent evidence has provided us a better understanding of the molecular nature of alpha-thalassemia in Saudi Arabia, with the most frequent abnormality being the deletional form −α 3.7 (62.3%), followed by α2 IVS1(−5nt) (20.7%) and the mutational form α2 polyA-1 (α2 T. Saudi ) (14.1%) ( 18–21 ).

bc7610d2-10d8-4a15-b6b0-c8f624d46d14.text:
Linear regression models were constructed for continuous outcomes. Hemoglobin was adjusted for age, sex, and the presence of HbS; MCV was adjusted for ferritin status (<50 vs. ≥ 50 μg/L) and the presence of HbS. Other CBC parameters (MCH, MCHC, RDW, and RBC count) and hemoglobin variants (HbA, HbA2, HbF, and HbH) were adjusted for the presence of HbS. Ferritin was also adjusted for age and sex.

Logistic regression models were used for binary outcomes as follows: transfusion history adjusted for age, sex, and HbS status. Low ferritin (<50 μg/L) adjusted for age and sex. Low MCV (<80 fL) adjusted for ferritin status and HbS presence.

Both univariate and multivariate odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were reported. To test the hypothesis that low ferritin affects MCV differently in the deletion versus mutation groups, we conducted a linear regression analysis with an interaction term (genetic group × ferritin status) with pairwise comparisons using the Bonferroni-corrected pairwise t -tests.

25137477-88f1-481d-b570-af419882d526.text:
A total of 378 patients with genetically confirmed alpha-thalassemia were included in the study. Patients were categorized into three groups: the deletion group (n = 276) included patients with deletions only with no mutations, the mutation group (n = 64) included patients with mutations only with no deletions, and the mixed/other group (n = 38) included patients with both deletions and mutations. The primary analysis compared the 340 patients included in the deletion and mutation groups without patients with both abnormalities.

A significant interaction was found between low ferritin and MCV, which indicates that the effect of low ferritin on MCV differs between genetic groups. Low ferritin substantially reduced MCV in the deletion group ( p < 0.001) but had no significant effect in the mutation group ( p = 0.707), supporting the hypothesis that mutations preserve MCV despite iron deficiency ( Table 5 ).

Figure 2 shows the frequency of different genotype subgroups identified in our study. More details about these genotypes are shown in Table 6 .

a4c88aea-bb33-4b5f-b2fa-d71593abc572.paper_title: Genotype–phenotype correlation in alpha-thalassemia: predicting genetic subgroups via laboratory parameters
a4c88aea-bb33-4b5f-b2fa-d71593abc572.text:
To the best of our knowledge, our study is one of the largest, if not the largest, cohorts of genetically confirmed alpha-thalassemia reported from a single center in our region.

Our study has reported that RDW elevation in the mutational group was 1.67% higher than that seen in the deletional group ( p = 0.006), indicating greater red cell size variability in the mutational subtype, which is independent of HbS status. We have also shown that HbH is the strongest discriminator between the genetic types, as it is dramatically elevated in the mutational group, in which it was 1.59% higher than the deletional group ( p < 0.001) with a very high odds ratio (unadjusted = 21.49 and adjusted for the presence of HbS = 1.59). Furthermore, our analysis has shown a unique finding that iron deficiency affects the MCV in the two genetic types differently, suggesting distinct underlying physiologic pathways. Patients with low ferritin and the deletional type had a statistically significant difference in the mean MCV as compared to those with normal ferritin (68.1 versus 72.2, p -value = <0.001), but the same difference was not observed in the mutational group (68.7 versus 66.2, p -value = 0.707).

665057cd-f1d9-4769-b713-b0f2775c927f.text: Liver cancer is a significant global health issue, with more than 8,50,000 new cases reported annually [ 1 ]. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for 75–85% of primary liver cancer cases, while intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma accounts for 10–15% of cases, along with other rarer forms [ 2 , 3 ]. Several well-established risk factors contribute to the development of HCC, including cirrhosis (chronic liver damage caused by fibrosis), hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, alcohol abuse, and metabolic syndrome. [ [4] , [5] , [6] ]. The incidence of HCC varies significantly across countries, primarily due to differences in the prevalence of risk factors. Regardless of the underlying etiology, these conditions often lead to liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, which eventually progress to carcinoma. Liver cancer is the sixth most commonly diagnosed cancer and the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, with approximately 8,65,269 new cases and 7,57,948 deaths annually [ 7 ]. Liver cancer occurs most frequently in males aged 50 to 69 years, while in females, the highest incidence is observed after the age of 70 years [ 8 ]. Men are generally more affected than women, contributing to a lower overall survival rate worldwide.

22513c93-d083-49de-8ad0-d1ffcb9d2412.text: The patient is a known case of hypertension for the past 10 years on regular medication, tablet Concor 5 mg and tablet Telma 40 mg, OD each. c9cf0594-acbd-46b8-818d-3eed4fdf4de6.paper_title: A recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma with incomplete response to conventional treatments, showing substantial regression and good quality of life by Ayurveda treatment: A case report
c9cf0594-acbd-46b8-818d-3eed4fdf4de6.text: The patient's diagnosis of HCC was established through a series of imaging studies and laboratory investigations. An abdominal ultrasound, followed by a contrast-enhanced MRI, identified a hepatic mass, helped for the probable diagnosis of the disease as carcinoma. Liver function tests indicated impaired liver function, with elevated bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels. A tumor marker analysis showed a significantly high alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) level, a strong indicator of HCC. To confirm the diagnosis, a liver biopsy was needed. But in view of the nature and location of the lesion, it could not be undertaken. So diagnosis was made as per the results of imaging, tumor markers and bio-chemistry. Endoscopic evaluations detected bile duct obstruction caused by tumor compression, making stenting necessary. This comprehensive assessment provided a clear understanding of the patient's condition and allowed for an informed approach to treatment.

6243f014-3333-4d5e-aa0e-19e3d7b394e4.paper_title: A recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma with incomplete response to conventional treatments, showing substantial regression and good quality of life by Ayurveda treatment: A case report
6243f014-3333-4d5e-aa0e-19e3d7b394e4.text:
After the conventional treatments, the patient was treated with an Ayurvedic regimen starting February 20, 2024, which included s uvarna malini v asant a , p halatrikadi g uggulu , p atol a , b humyamalaki , and b hring a raj a to support liver function, improve digestion, detoxify the body, and reduce inflammation ( Table 2 ). Given his obesity (108 kg at diagnosis), and currently 102 kg, a liver-supporting diet, low in fatty, spicy, and non-vegetarian foods, was recommended for weight management and digestive health, with nutritional counselling to avoid strain on the liver.

With limited physical activity, a rehabilitation plan incorporating light exercises such as walking and stretching was introduced to improve mobility and prevent muscle atrophy. Psychosocial support, including counselling and stress-relief techniques, was advised to address emotional challenges related to his diagnosis.

Regular monitoring of liver function tests, tumor markers and imaging studies to track HCC progression, and attention to potential complications like ascites, jaundice and bleeding were provided. This comprehensive treatment strategy, integrating conventional and Ayurvedic therapies, along with dietary, physical, and emotional support, aimed to improve the patient's quality of life, manage symptoms, and slow down the disease progression.

6429b487-41e6-4898-ab09-ac1dfab77dd2.paper_title: A recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma with incomplete response to conventional treatments, showing substantial regression and good quality of life by Ayurveda treatment: A case report
6429b487-41e6-4898-ab09-ac1dfab77dd2.text: The patient experienced significant improvements after resuming Ayurvedic therapy, both clinical as well as pathological. Previously patient had discontinued tablet Lenvatinib because of severe side effects, and his AFP was raised to 10.3 in Feb 2024 from 6.36 in Dec 2023. The oncologist suggested to check it again after one month, and if it remains high, then had advocated the need of restarting tablet Lenvatinib but Ayurved treatment was immediately started and the AFP value on 31 March came down to 7.95, so tablet Lenvatinib was kept on hold, and now AFP has always remained below 5.5 for last many months. So, tablet Lenvatinib was never started. Total bilirubin also came down to 1.2 mg/ from 2 mg/ in Feb 2024, and reduced further to 1.1 mg in May 2025. AST, ALT and Alkaline phosphatase were fairly in range.
6429b487-41e6-4898-ab09-ac1dfab77dd2.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and Integrative Medicine

c5b53162-c176-42ff-a3be-6fd47530cfc2.text: Based on this rationale, a novel paradigm for identification is proposed: the combined use of TMAO and PAGln as dual biomarkers for DKD. The measurement of individual biomarkers often exhibits inherent limitations in sensitivity or specificity. When one biomarker is near its clinical threshold, an aberrant level of the other provides orthogonal validation, reducing failure to identify DKD and misclassification. This integrated approach could improve identification rates and classification precision.

f0cd05b1-4945-42e4-ab7b-1c3477b9c43b.paper_title: Trimethylamine N-Oxide Combined with Phenylacetylglutamine as Potential Biomarkers for Diabetic Kidney Disease
f0cd05b1-4945-42e4-ab7b-1c3477b9c43b.text: In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 165 consecutive patients with T2DM were recruited from the Department of Nephrology at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University between December 2023 and June 2024. To minimize selection bias, all eligible participants during this period were included using a consecutive sampling method. The cohort consisted of 63 patients with T2DM but without kidney disease and 102 patients with DKD. DKD was defined as the presence of UACR ≥ 30 mg/g and/or eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m 2 in patients with type 2 diabetes, after excluding other causes of kidney damage. Plasma concentrations of TMAO and PAGln were quantified at Changsha Duxact Biotech Co., Ltd.

726e490e-b18d-412b-997d-c1d26f5d20ac.text: This study enrolled a total of 165 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, comprising 63 patients without nephropathy (52.4% male, mean age 59 years) and 102 patients with DKD (76.5% male, mean age 60 years). As summarized in Table 1 , significant differences in baseline clinical characteristics and laboratory parameters were observed between the two groups. Specifically, the DKD group demonstrated more pronounced cardiovascular and metabolic disturbances, as evidenced by higher systolic SBP, DBP, and blood glucose levels. GLU and HbA1c levels were significantly elevated in patients with DKD compared to those with T2DM alone. In terms of lipid profiles, TC, LDL-C, and HDL-C were significantly reduced in the DKD group.

6e52d828-60e5-4c55-a414-13fb92f03229.heading_path: Results > Correlation of TMAO and PAGln with Renal Function Indicators
6e52d828-60e5-4c55-a414-13fb92f03229.text: The assessment of renal function relies on several key indicators, including Scr, BUN, and eGFR, all of which reflect glomerular filtration capacity. Urinary indices that serve as direct markers of renal dysfunction include MAU and the UACR. Among markers of uric acid metabolism, serum UA level primarily reflects renal excretory capacity. As shown in Table 2 and Figure 2 , plasma TMAO levels demonstrated significant positive correlations with BUN (r = 0.610), Scr (r = 0.617), UA (r = 0.379), MAU (r = 0.303), and UACR (r = 0.323) ( P < 0.01), and a significant inverse correlation with eGFR (r = −0.616, P < 0.001). Collectively, these findings indicate that TMAO may hold potential value for identifying DKD.

b9b08076-4421-4c38-b53a-04bb343d016f.heading_path: Results > Progressive Elevation of TMAO and PAGln Across Declining eGFR Categories
b9b08076-4421-4c38-b53a-04bb343d016f.text: To examine the relationship between gut microbiota-derived metabolites and renal function in T2DM, patients were stratified into three eGFR categories: ≥60, 30–59, and <30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 . Both TMAO and PAGln exhibited a marked stepwise increase with declining eGFR ( Table 4 ), with the highest levels observed in patients with severe renal impairment ( P < 0.001). These findings indicate that circulating TMAO and PAGln rise progressively as renal function deteriorates.

bc2a1e0a-ab3d-489d-9b66-fcb0d6ae994a.paper_title: Trimethylamine N-Oxide Combined with Phenylacetylglutamine as Potential Biomarkers for Diabetic Kidney Disease
bc2a1e0a-ab3d-489d-9b66-fcb0d6ae994a.heading_path: Results > Identification Value of Combined TMAO and PAGln for DKD
bc2a1e0a-ab3d-489d-9b66-fcb0d6ae994a.text: ROC curve analysis was conducted to evaluate the ability of TMAO and PAGln, both individually and in combination, to identify DKD. Specificity, sensitivity, the AUC, and optimal cutoff values were calculated. As summarized in Table 5 and Figure 3 , the AUC of TMAO for identifying DKD was 0.795, with a sensitivity of 65.7% and a specificity of 92.1% at the optimal cutoff value (corresponding to a plasma TMAO level of 5.257 μM) determined by the maximum Youden index. For PAGln, the AUC was 0.832, with a sensitivity of 68.3% and a specificity of 88.5% at the optimal cutoff (plasma PAGln level of 3.64 μM) based on the maximum Youden index. The combination of TMAO and PAGln achieved a significantly higher AUC of 0.846 for identifying DKD, with a substantial increase in sensitivity (75.6%) while maintaining high specificity (85.2%).

aa19a99e-6e4b-4a93-bada-1e568c0de5cd.paper_title: Trimethylamine N-Oxide Combined with Phenylacetylglutamine as Potential Biomarkers for Diabetic Kidney Disease
aa19a99e-6e4b-4a93-bada-1e568c0de5cd.text: DKD is a prevalent microvascular complication of diabetes and a leading cause of ESKD and cardiovascular mortality worldwide. Consequently, identification and regular assessment are crucial for mitigating disease progression. Conventional biomarkers, such as MAU, SCr, BUN, and eGFR, are associated with well-documented limitations. Their identification specificity and accuracy are often compromised by susceptibility to various confounding factors, including acute infections, strenuous exercise, hemorrhage, and exposure to nephrotoxic agents. 30 , 31 Therefore, identifying novel biomarkers to accurately assess DKD prognosis is imperative. Such biomarkers are needed to enhance identification precision, reduce under‑identification, facilitate early intervention, and allow dynamic monitoring of disease progression, thereby optimizing therapeutic strategies.

eb74000e-5dee-4994-9fd4-d7955b748209.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
eb74000e-5dee-4994-9fd4-d7955b748209.text: Human serum albumin (HSA) is the most abundant protein in serum, accounting for approximately 60%–65% of total serum proteins [ 1 ]. It plays pivotal roles in diverse physiological functions, including maintenance of colloid osmotic pressure, transport of long-chain fatty acids and drugs, and antioxidant activity as a radical scavenger [ 1 ]. Approximately 10–15 g of HSA is synthesized daily in the liver, maintaining a plasma half-life of approximately 20 days as it circulates between the intravascular space and the interstitial fluid [ 1 ]. During this prolonged circulation, HSA sensitively reflects the internal milieu and undergoes various post-translational modifications (PTMs), including oxidation, glycation, carbamylation, truncation, and dimerization [ 2–4 ].

b946e05d-4d9b-4d97-810f-b785d22e02d0.text: Extensive studies have established that Cys34 undergoes diverse oxidative modifications—including nitrosylation, sulfenylation, sulfonylation, and cysteinylation—in response to systemic oxidative stress, and the oxidized fraction of Cys34 has been proposed as a sensitive biomarker for ageing and oxidative stress–related diseases. fd3a9c46-c895-4e4d-9ac3-67898b5b87e6.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
fd3a9c46-c895-4e4d-9ac3-67898b5b87e6.heading_path: Albumin structure and redox states > Discovery of HSA polysulfides as endogenous supersulfides
fd3a9c46-c895-4e4d-9ac3-67898b5b87e6.text:
Extensive studies have established that Cys34 undergoes diverse oxidative modifications—including nitrosylation, sulfenylation, sulfonylation, and cysteinylation—in response to systemic oxidative stress, and the oxidized fraction of Cys34 has been proposed as a sensitive biomarker for ageing and oxidative stress–related diseases. However, several observations challenge the traditional view that albumin's redox activity is regulated by Cys34 alone. Recombinant albumin mutants lacking Cys34 retain substantial antioxidative activity, indicating the involvement of additional redox-active elements beyond Cys34 [ 11 ]. Furthermore, specific intramolecular cysteine–cysteine bridges, including Cys392–Cys438 and Cys558–Cys567, exhibit redox or chemical reactivity that cannot be readily explained by classical disulfide chemistry [ 12 , 13 ].

Reduced-form polysulfides (Red-PSS), which are prevalent in intracellular proteins, have been extensively studied owing to the availability of alkylation-based assays and sulfane sulfur probes. In contrast, Ox-PSS remained poorly characterized for many years due to the lack of reliable quantitative methods, and its biological significance in extracellular proteins, such as albumin, was consequently overlooked.
fd3a9c46-c895-4e4d-9ac3-67898b5b87e6.journal: Redox Report : Communications in Free Radical Research

d1f1d597-f607-4123-b7b6-b8186358aa37.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
d1f1d597-f607-4123-b7b6-b8186358aa37.heading_path: Analytical advances > Advances in measurement technology: from HPLC to ESI-TOFMS
d1f1d597-f607-4123-b7b6-b8186358aa37.text:
High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was previously the primary method for evaluating the redox state of Cys34 [ 9 ]. Although HPLC has contributed substantially to pathophysiological analysis, it is limited by long measurement times and difficulty in identifying specific oxidative modification structures.

Methods developed using electrospray ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (ESI-TOFMS) have enabled high-sensitivity, high-throughput analysis of HSA PTMs [ 18–20 ]. This approach has revealed that the major molecular species of oxidized albumin is cysteinylated albumin (Cys-Cys34-HSA), in which a single cysteine molecule is attached to Cys34 ( Figure 3 ). The proportion of cysteinylated albumin measured by ESI-TOFMS shows a strong positive correlation with results from conventional HPLC methods, establishing it as a clinically applicable oxidative stress marker [ 18 ].
d1f1d597-f607-4123-b7b6-b8186358aa37.journal: Redox Report : Communications in Free Radical Research

5c6f16f9-578e-4d8e-9f0c-b73bcc61e12e.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
5c6f16f9-578e-4d8e-9f0c-b73bcc61e12e.heading_path: Analytical advances > Quantification of oxidized polysulfides in albumin
5c6f16f9-578e-4d8e-9f0c-b73bcc61e12e.text:
A major obstacle to elucidating the physiological role of Ox-PSS had been the absence of appropriate analytical tools. Conventional assays for hydrogen sulfide and sulfide ions—including the methylene blue method [ 21 ], electrode-based techniques, and derivatisation assays [ 22 ]—are not directly applicable to Ox-PSS embedded within protein structures. To overcome this limitation, the Elimination Method for Sulfide from Polysulfide (EMSP) was developed [ 23 ]. This approach exploits the susceptibility of Ox-PSS to alkaline hydrolysis, resulting in the release of sulfide ions that are quantitatively detected under stabilized conditions; ascorbic acid is employed to prevent sulfide oxidation during the assay.

Application of EMSP to purified HSA revealed that a single albumin molecule endogenously contains approximately 15 mol/mol of Ox-PSS–derived sulfide [ 23 ]. Comparative analyses across diverse proteins demonstrated a strong correlation between Ox-PSS content and cysteine residue number, whereas no such correlation was observed with methionine content. This finding provides the first direct evidence that polysulfide bridges are abundant structural features of albumin rather than rare post-translational modifications. Complementary mass spectrometric analyses further suggest that multiple intramolecular cysteine–cysteine bridges participate in polysulfide bond formation [ 24 ].
5c6f16f9-578e-4d8e-9f0c-b73bcc61e12e.journal: Redox Report : Communications in Free Radical Research

b8145f6f-99fa-47c5-90c3-a69c698686f6.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
b8145f6f-99fa-47c5-90c3-a69c698686f6.heading_path: Albumin polysulfides: functional significance and redox mechanism > Effect of polysulfides on albumin structure and function
b8145f6f-99fa-47c5-90c3-a69c698686f6.text:
To clarify the functional significance of albumin polysulfides, selectively and partially Ox-PSS–depleted albumin preparations were generated using Sulfane Sulfur Probe 4. Partial depletion was employed to avoid albumin aggregation. Even partial removal of Ox-PSS induced detectable alterations in both secondary and tertiary structures as assessed by circular dichroism spectroscopy, accompanied by increased exposure of hydrophobic surface regions, indicating destabilization of the native conformation. Functionally, partial Ox-PSS depletion markedly impaired albumin's drug-binding capacity at Site II—the binding site responsible for a wide range of acidic and neutral drugs at subdomain IIIA of HSA [ 25 ]. Reductions in Site II binding capacity have also been reported in oxidative stress–related diseases, such as acute kidney injury and chronic kidney or liver disease [ 26 , 27 ], suggesting that reduced albumin polysulfides may contribute to disease-related changes in pharmacokinetics and an increased incidence of drug side effects.

In addition to drug binding, removal of even a small fraction of Ox-PSS significantly reduced albumin's antioxidative activity, including hydrogen peroxide scavenging and free radical quenching, indicating that specific polysulfide sites may play dominant roles in redox buffering.
b8145f6f-99fa-47c5-90c3-a69c698686f6.journal: Redox Report : Communications in Free Radical Research

b39afb77-cf0b-46d8-858a-4ba39976bdda.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
b39afb77-cf0b-46d8-858a-4ba39976bdda.heading_path: Albumin polysulfides: functional significance and redox mechanism > Dynamic polysulfide redox cycling
b39afb77-cf0b-46d8-858a-4ba39976bdda.text: A recent report demonstrated that Ox-PSS reacts directly with reactive oxygen species (ROS) to be converted to Red-PSS, which transiently enhances antioxidant activity [ 24 ]. Under sustained pathological oxidative stress, irreversible oxidation of albumin occurs through consumption of Red-PSS, leading to a progressive decline in both antioxidant capacity and drug-binding capacity ( Figure 4 ). These findings demonstrate the existence of a novel in vivo redox regulation mechanism mediated by albumin polysulfides and establish HSA as a dynamic Ox-PSS reservoir capable of responding to fluctuating redox conditions.

363b1d34-e26d-4f67-b157-b5ae8e7d6864.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
363b1d34-e26d-4f67-b157-b5ae8e7d6864.heading_path: Albumin polysulfides: functional significance and redox mechanism > Dynamic polysulfide redox cycling
363b1d34-e26d-4f67-b157-b5ae8e7d6864.text:
A recent report demonstrated that Ox-PSS reacts directly with reactive oxygen species (ROS) to be converted to Red-PSS, which transiently enhances antioxidant activity [ 24 ]. Under sustained pathological oxidative stress, irreversible oxidation of albumin occurs through consumption of Red-PSS, leading to a progressive decline in both antioxidant capacity and drug-binding capacity ( Figure 4 ). These findings demonstrate the existence of a novel in vivo redox regulation mechanism mediated by albumin polysulfides and establish HSA as a dynamic Ox-PSS reservoir capable of responding to fluctuating redox conditions.

Taken together, albumin-bound polysulfides emerge as a critical and previously underappreciated component of extracellular redox regulation. Their capacity to directly quench ROS, interface with systemic sulfur metabolism, and influence downstream thiol oxidation supports a multilayered defense network that sustains redox homeostasis. When this system is disrupted under pathological oxidative stress, the consequences extend beyond a loss of antioxidant buffering to include impairment of albumin's ligand-binding and transport functions, thereby potentially contributing to disease progression and altering therapeutic outcomes.

2d8866a2-1f6c-48f9-ac86-040d96286cc3.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
2d8866a2-1f6c-48f9-ac86-040d96286cc3.text: In the field of nephrology in particular, oxidized albumin could be emerging not only as a biomarker but also as a therapeutic target and active pathogenic substance. The evidence reviewed in this section encompasses a diverse range of study designs, spanning from longitudinal human cohorts (e.g. the PREVEND study [ 28 ]), and cross-sectional observational data to in vitro and animal models. Consequently, the strength of causal inference derived from these findings varies accordingly. It should be explicitly noted that oxidized albumin may function as a biomarker, a mediator, or an epiphenomenon depending on the clinical context. This distinction remains incompletely resolved for most of the conditions discussed herein.
2d8866a2-1f6c-48f9-ac86-040d96286cc3.journal: Redox Report : Communications in Free Radical Research

25feeeae-effb-464f-84e9-75788ec4a061.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
25feeeae-effb-464f-84e9-75788ec4a061.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular risk
25feeeae-effb-464f-84e9-75788ec4a061.text: A 10-year follow-up study of 4745 healthy individuals (the PREVEND study) demonstrated that lower serum free thiol levels are significantly associated with a higher risk of developing CKD [ 28 ]. Since approximately 80% of these thiol groups originate from Cys34, a decrease in thiol content reflects a shift from reduced to oxidized albumin, suggesting that systemic oxidative stress and accumulation of modified albumin are associated with renal decline, though whether oxidative modification of albumin is a driver, accelerant, or consequence of disease progression has not been established in interventional studies. It is well established that HMA decreases and oxidized albumin (HNA1, HNA2) increases as renal function declines in patients with non-dialysis CKD and those on dialysis [ 9 , 29 , 30 ]. Low HMA levels in dialysis patients significantly correlate with the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) onset and CVD-related mortality, consistent with a contribution of oxidative stress to atherosclerosis progression, though causality remains to be demonstrated. Additionally, in peritoneal dialysis patients, higher serum HMA levels have been reported to correlate with higher peritoneal transport status [ 31 ].

dd066591-b5e6-4420-b93c-8064a48eadd6.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
dd066591-b5e6-4420-b93c-8064a48eadd6.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Highly oxidized albumin in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
dd066591-b5e6-4420-b93c-8064a48eadd6.text: In patients with active focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), highly oxidized albumin—in which Cys34 is irreversibly oxidized to sulfonic acid (─SO₃H)—has been specifically detected in plasma [ 32 ]. This oxidative modification correlates with disease activity and may be useful for predicting recurrence after transplantation.

c10f68a3-c491-473e-8c11-8b512df44f69.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
c10f68a3-c491-473e-8c11-8b512df44f69.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Prognostic prediction in diabetic kidney disease and diabetic retinopathy
c10f68a3-c491-473e-8c11-8b512df44f69.text: Cysteinylated albumin has been shown to predict early progression of diabetic kidney disease (DKD)—specifically the transition from stage G2 to G3a—with higher accuracy than urinary albumin excretion [ 33 ]. Regarding diabetic retinopathy [ 34 ], a 2025 exploratory retrospective cohort pilot study demonstrated that baseline HNA% in patients with simple diabetic retinopathy was associated with improvement in retinopathy after 5 years [ 35 ]. The baseline HNA% was significantly lower in the improvement group, and this association was independent of HbA1c levels during follow-up, suggesting that HNA% may reflect cumulative oxidative stress, including past glycaemic fluctuations (the legacy effect)—a prognostic dimension distinct from HbA1c. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

ce4821a7-a24a-46d8-a410-b310e03420bc.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
ce4821a7-a24a-46d8-a410-b310e03420bc.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Alport syndrome and Nrf2 activation therapy
ce4821a7-a24a-46d8-a410-b310e03420bc.text: A 2025 study by Kaseda et al. demonstrated that UD-051, an Nrf2 activator (Keap1–Nrf2 interaction inhibitor), dose-dependently suppressed decline in renal function, glomerular sclerosis, inflammation, and fibrosis in a mouse model of Alport syndrome, thereby extending survival [ 36 ]. Plasma oxidized albumin ratio showed a strong inverse correlation with expression levels of Nrf2 target genes ( Nqo1 , Gclc ) in renal tissue, indicating that plasma oxidized albumin is a sensitive biomarker reflecting antioxidant capacity (Nrf2 activity) within renal tissue.

0d70d3d8-59a0-4807-9a28-6ac66e7031e4.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
0d70d3d8-59a0-4807-9a28-6ac66e7031e4.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Induction of ferroptosis: a novel pathogenic mechanism
0d70d3d8-59a0-4807-9a28-6ac66e7031e4.text: Although it has long been suggested that oxidized albumin possesses intrinsic toxicity capable of exacerbating renal damage, a 2025 study identified ferroptosis as the specific underlying mechanism [ 37 ]. Exposure of renal tubular epithelial cells (NRK-52E) to oxidized albumin induced cell death characterized by intracellular albumin accumulation, increased lipid peroxidation, intracellular iron accumulation, and decreased expression of antioxidant factors GPX4 and xCT, together with increased expression of the lipid metabolism enzyme ACSL4; these changes were suppressed by ferroptosis inhibitors. Administration of oxidized albumin to a doxorubicin-induced nephropathy mouse model exacerbated renal function, proteinuria, and tubular injury in vivo. These findings raise the possibility that oxidized albumin may function not merely as a consequence of oxidative stress but as an active contributor to renal tubular injury. However, these conclusions are based on a single preclinical study using one cell line and one mouse model; independent replication across a range of nephropathy models and, ultimately, clinical validation will be required before the ferroptosis mechanism can be established as a general pathogenic pathway.
0d70d3d8-59a0-4807-9a28-6ac66e7031e4.journal: Redox Report : Communications in Free Radical Research

d8f94390-247d-4f8e-af6c-d960ce20f054.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
d8f94390-247d-4f8e-af6c-d960ce20f054.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Impact of AOPPs on renal health and sarcopenia
d8f94390-247d-4f8e-af6c-d960ce20f054.text: Advanced oxidation protein products (AOPPs) are formed when hypochlorous acid (HOCl), produced by neutrophils during inflammation, oxidatively modifies serum proteins—primarily albumin. AOPPs trigger tubular disorders by inducing abnormal fatty acid metabolism in renal cells [ 38 ] and contribute to muscle wasting and weakness (sarcopenia) by causing mitochondrial dysfunction in skeletal muscle [ 39 , 40 ]. Serum AOPPs and oxidized albumin levels are significantly elevated in dialysis patients with sarcopenia compared with those without [ 39 ], suggesting utility as diagnostic tools for sarcopenia in the CKD population. Since the link between AOPPs and sarcopenia is supported by mechanistic data from animal models [ 39 , 40 ] and human cross-sectional associations [ 39 ], further longitudinal or interventional studies in humans are warranted.

c9960ed1-dacb-4b26-a655-badb32aa54b5.heading_path: Pathophysiological significance > Decline of functional albumin in liver disease
c9960ed1-dacb-4b26-a655-badb32aa54b5.text:
In chronic liver disease (CLD), cysteinylated albumin increases progressively with advancing Child–Pugh classification stage [ 18 , 41 ]. Oxidatively modified HSA exhibits reduced binding affinity for bilirubin and drugs, including warfarin and diazepam, impairing its function as ‘functional albumin’ [ 18 , 27 , 34 , 41 , 42 ]. Administration of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) preparations has been confirmed not only to promote albumin production but also to restore the proportion of HMA and improve ligand-binding capacity [ 18 , 41 ], demonstrating that therapeutic intervention can produce measurable qualitative improvement in circulating albumin.

A critical caveat applies across the pathophysiological evidence reviewed in this section. With few exceptions, associations between albumin oxidation and disease outcomes derive from observational human studies, in vitro experiments, or limited animal models. These data are insufficient to establish definitively whether oxidized albumin functions as a causative driver, a consequential biomarker, or an innocent bystander in disease pathogenesis. Human interventional studies demonstrating that restoration of reduced albumin or prevention of Cys34 oxidation translates into improved clinical outcomes are largely absent and represent an important research priority. Until such evidence is available, claims about the pathogenic role of oxidized albumin should be interpreted with appropriate caution.

f4aa6e37-4631-46df-a278-d289a06eee76.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
f4aa6e37-4631-46df-a278-d289a06eee76.heading_path: Clinical and pharmaceutical applications > Reduced albumin as a sensitive biomarker for nutrition and physical function
f4aa6e37-4631-46df-a278-d289a06eee76.text: Two recent studies highlight the proportion of reduced albumin as a more sensitive indicator of health status in older adults than total serum albumin concentration. Motokawa et al. reported that while conventional serum albumin levels in community-dwelling older adults do not correlate with protein intake, the ratio of reduced albumin is significantly associated with insufficient dietary protein intake, suggesting its utility as an indicator of mild malnutrition [ 43 ]. Shibasaki et al. demonstrated that reduced albumin is linked to physical function during resistance training interventions in middle-aged and older adults; a positive correlation was observed between improvement in maximum walking speed and the increase in reduced albumin following training [ 44 ]. Together, these findings suggest that reduced albumin reflects both protein nutritional status and motor function or training efficacy in older adults.

3e14c97d-1f82-4916-80d7-81aebc8fcfa2.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
3e14c97d-1f82-4916-80d7-81aebc8fcfa2.heading_path: Clinical and pharmaceutical applications > Clinical implications of albumin polysulfides
3e14c97d-1f82-4916-80d7-81aebc8fcfa2.text:
Oxidative stress is a hallmark of numerous chronic diseases, including CKD, CLD, cardiovascular disease, and chronic inflammatory disorders [ 45 ]. Clinical studies have demonstrated that polysulfide levels in circulating albumin are significantly reduced in patients with CKD compared with healthy controls. Notably, polysulfide levels increase rapidly following hemodialysis, reflecting the removal of oxidative stress–inducing substances, such as ROS and uremic toxins, highlighting the dynamic responsiveness of albumin polysulfides to systemic redox conditions [ 46 ].

Beyond CKD, alterations in albumin redox state have been reported in CLD, sepsis, and acute inflammatory conditions [ 26 , 27 ]. Importantly, serum polysulfides are significantly reduced in patients with early hepatitis in the context of CLD, even when the mercaptoalbumin ratio—a conventional oxidative stress marker—remains unchanged ( Figure 5 ). This observation suggests that albumin polysulfide assessment may provide additional qualitative information that enhances risk stratification and disease monitoring at earlier stages of oxidative stress than conventional Cys34-based markers allow. Low serum albumin levels have also been associated with poor outcomes in severe infections, such as COVID-19 [ 47 , 48 ]; in this context, assessment of albumin polysulfide content may offer further qualitative insight beyond total albumin concentration.

1ccf83a2-7dfe-4ddc-95e5-562db89ad473.text: The degree of PTMs in clinical albumin preparations may vary depending on manufacturing processes and storage conditions. Comparative analyses of commercial preparations have demonstrated that preparations with a higher proportion of cysteinylated albumin exhibit lower ligand-binding and antioxidant capacities [ 49 ], indicating that the degree of Cys34 oxidation may be a useful quality indicator for evaluating the functional quality of such preparations.

14099b74-b6d4-4d0c-b26d-fac6fa83ead4.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
14099b74-b6d4-4d0c-b26d-fac6fa83ead4.heading_path: Clinical and pharmaceutical applications > Pharmacological and biopharmaceutical perspectives
14099b74-b6d4-4d0c-b26d-fac6fa83ead4.text:
From a pharmaceutical standpoint, albumin polysulfides have important implications for drug development and therapy. Albumin is widely exploited as a drug carrier through both non-covalent binding and covalent conjugation strategies. Changes in albumin structure and binding properties resulting from altered polysulfide content may therefore influence drug distribution, efficacy, and toxicity. Furthermore, modulation of albumin polysulfides represents a potential therapeutic strategy: enhancement of polysulfide content may improve albumin's antioxidative capacity and stabilize drug-binding functions under pathological conditions. Proof-of-concept has already been demonstrated—albumin with increased polysulfide content has been engineered to alleviate kidney injury in a rhabdomyolysis model [ 50 ].

Albumin polysulfides represent a previously unrecognized qualitative dimension of albumin redox biology that extends our understanding beyond classical antioxidant mechanisms. Further evidence will clarify how albumin functions as a dynamic polysulfide reservoir contributing to systemic redox homeostasis and influencing both drug-binding and antioxidant properties.

175218bc-e528-4335-b3e2-8e67f6e944a5.paper_title: Albumin as a dynamic extracellular redox regulator: from Cys34 oxidation biomarkers to polysulfide-mediated homeostatic mechanisms and clinical applications
175218bc-e528-4335-b3e2-8e67f6e944a5.text:
The framework of ‘redox albuminomics’ provides a crucial approach for evaluating qualitative changes in HSA—particularly the oxidation state of Cys34—as sensitive biomarkers of systemic oxidative stress. Advanced analytical techniques, such as ESI-TOFMS, have enhanced our ability to identify specific oxidative modifications, establishing oxidized albumin as a clinically relevant marker across a range of diseases. Beyond its role as a biomarker, oxidized albumin exhibits intrinsic pathogenicity in CKD, contributing to cardiovascular risk, sarcopenia, and—as recently demonstrated—ferroptosis-mediated renal tubular cell death. Its utility further extends to nutritional and physical function assessment in older adults and to pharmaceutical quality control.

Complementing this established biology, the assessment and regulation of albumin polysulfides opens new opportunities for biomarker development and therapeutic intervention in oxidative stress–related diseases. Albumin polysulfides are dynamically regulated, respond more sensitively than Cys34-based markers at early disease stages, and directly influence drug-binding and antioxidant function. Future research targeting oxidized albumin and albumin polysulfides as therapeutic objectives holds significant potential for improving clinical outcomes. Advances in protein polysulfide measurement techniques and the development of agents that promote albumin polysulfide formation are anticipated to become increasingly important research priorities.

bdb5f045-9e45-4682-8dd4-7f873a08b55c.paper_title: Thrombocytopenia and anemia associated with piperacillin-tazobactam: integrating clinical case series with FAERS disproportionality analysis
bdb5f045-9e45-4682-8dd4-7f873a08b55c.text:
Piperacillin, commonly used in combination with β-lactamase inhibitors (e.g., tazobactam), is a broad-spectrum antibiotic and a first-line empiric therapy for moderate to severe infections in hospitalized patients due to its efficacy and generally favorable tolerability profile ( Young and Plosker, 2001 ; Gin et al., 2007 ). Despite the widespread clinical use of piperacillin-tazobactam (TZP), the risk of haematopoietic toxicity and its potentially serious consequences cannot be overlooked ( Wang et al., 2020 ; Gerhardy et al., 2021 ).

To address these evidence gaps, pharmacovigilance databases such as the U.S. FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) are invaluable. Through disproportionality analysis, these repositories can transform sporadic clinical observations into quantifiable risk signals, enabling the detection of rare adverse drug reactions ( Morris et al., 2024 ). However, database analyses alone often lack detailed clinical context.

6f5ac581-22d4-4c21-849e-1c10c5eebe0d.heading_path: Case descriptions > Case 2: severe anemia accompanied by mild thrombocytopenia
6f5ac581-22d4-4c21-849e-1c10c5eebe0d.text: A 54-year-old female with type 2 diabetes was admitted on 13 October 2025, for a diabetic foot infection complicated by ketoacidosis. She had a 3-year history of elevated blood glucose and presented with right foot ulceration for 1 week. She had a 3-year history of hypertension but did not take medication regularly, and denied history of coronary heart disease or other chronic conditions. On admission, vital signs were as follows: temperature 36.3 °C, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, heart rate 101 beats/min, and blood pressure 112/71 mmHg. Laboratory findings included white blood cell count 25.93 × 10 9 /L, neutrophil percentage 89.3%, red blood cell count 3.15 × 10 12 /L, CRP 125.6 mg/L, PCT 1.11 ng/mL, unconjugated bilirubin 38.8 μmol/L, total bilirubin 39.5 μmol/L, and blood ketone 1.2 mmol/L. Her baseline hemoglobin level at presentation was 92 g/L. Intravenous TZP (4.5 g every 8 h) was initiated after admission. Concomitant medications included insulin aspart injection, lipoic acid injection, moxifloxacin sodium chloride injection, and nifedipine controlled-release tablets.

7c7677a0-c491-448d-aff2-9427671cc00a.text:
On 4 January 2026, based on the patient’s blood culture results, which revealed Escherichia coli resistant to second-generation cephalosporins and susceptible to TZP, the antimicrobial therapy was switched from cefotetan to intravenous TZP (2.25 g every 8 h). Within 3 days of initiating TZP, the hemoglobin level dropped to 85 g/L on January 7 in the absence of bleeding. On the same day, repeat laboratory tests showed white blood cell count 11.20 × 10 9 /L, neutrophil percentage 71.4%, red blood cell count 2.73 × 10 12 /L, and PCT 0.25 ng/mL, unconjugated bilirubin 3.9 μmol/L, total bilirubin 12.3 μmol/L. The patient’s clinical symptoms and inflammatory markers improved, indicating that the infection was effectively controlled, despite a marked decrease in red blood cell count and hemoglobin levels.

Causality Assessment: The hematological decline occurred specifically after the introduction of TZP, with stabilization on the prior antibiotic and recovery upon its discontinuation. This pattern supports a probable association (Naranjo score: 7, Supplementary Table S1 ).

cf8c230d-76ec-4811-9b98-702ebf7ee17c.paper_title: Thrombocytopenia and anemia associated with piperacillin-tazobactam: integrating clinical case series with FAERS disproportionality analysis
cf8c230d-76ec-4811-9b98-702ebf7ee17c.heading_path: FAERS database analysis results > Descriptive results for the population
cf8c230d-76ec-4811-9b98-702ebf7ee17c.text:
Following FDA-recommended data cleaning rules, a total of 9,066 TZP-related reports were identified from Q1 2004 to Q2 2025, involving 27,508 adverse drug events. Using the narrow Standardized Medical Queries (SMQs) for “Haematopoietic thrombocytopenia” (SMQ code: 20000031) and “Haematopoietic erythropenia” (SMQ code: 20000029), 501 reports of TZP-associated thrombocytopenia and 26 reports of TZP-associated anemia were identified. Details are presented in Supplementary Figure S1 .

bd5dbd0a-b3f0-4b40-bd5c-0b4dd1138297.heading_path: FAERS database analysis results > Sensitivity analysis
bd5dbd0a-b3f0-4b40-bd5c-0b4dd1138297.text: An analysis of concomitant medications in 501 reports of Haematopoietic thrombocytopenia under the SMQ identified a total of 505 drugs, with an average of 3.8 drugs per patient. The names and frequencies of these concomitant medications are shown in Supplementary Table S2 . We excluded 150 reports that involved nine drugs with well-established evidence of causing thrombocytopenia: vancomycin, heparin, enoxaparin, linezolid, dalteparin, carboplatin, quinine, cisplatin, and nadroparin. 9becacdc-e8ca-4ee3-abc4-6769b1cd444f.paper_title: Thrombocytopenia and anemia associated with piperacillin-tazobactam: integrating clinical case series with FAERS disproportionality analysis
9becacdc-e8ca-4ee3-abc4-6769b1cd444f.text: In this study, we combined detailed clinical case descriptions with a large-scale FAERS database disproportionality analysis to characterize TZP-associated haematopoietic toxicity. The key findings are threefold. First, the three presented cases illustrate distinct clinical phenotypes: severe thrombocytopenia with mild anemia (positive rechallenge), severe anemia with mild thrombocytopenia, and isolated anemia. Second, the FAERS disproportionality analysis revealed a strong, robust signal for TZP-associated thrombocytopenia, which remained stable after excluding reports with concomitant thrombocytopenic drugs. Third, in contrast, the signal for TZP-associated anemia was weak and did not meet predefined thresholds across all four detection methods, despite the occurrence of clinically significant anemia in our case series.

b0eefa0e-ee72-42bc-83c1-619dadb66c58.paper_title: Thrombocytopenia and anemia associated with piperacillin-tazobactam: integrating clinical case series with FAERS disproportionality analysis
b0eefa0e-ee72-42bc-83c1-619dadb66c58.text: TZP is associated with a strong and robust pharmacovigilance signal for thrombocytopenia, which remains stable after adjusting for concomitant medications. In contrast, the signal for TZP-associated anemia is weak in the FAERS database despite clear evidence of causality from clinical case series. This discrepancy likely reflects high background noise, underreporting, and individual susceptibility. Clinicians should maintain vigilance for both haematopoietic adverse events during TZP therapy, with particular attention to platelet, hemoglobin, and red blood cell levels within the first week of treatment. Unexplained cytopenias should prompt consideration of TZP as a potential cause, and timely discontinuation is warranted when drug-associated toxicity is suspected.

030727b7-1f86-469c-80aa-6ca81b1de359.paper_title: Thrombocytopenia and anemia associated with piperacillin-tazobactam: integrating clinical case series with FAERS disproportionality analysis
030727b7-1f86-469c-80aa-6ca81b1de359.text: This study combines two complementary components: (1) a single-center retrospective case series of patients with suspected TZP-associated hematologic adverse events, and (2) a pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis using the FAERS database. The case series component was conducted at a 1,000-bed urban tertiary hospital in Guangzhou, China, with clinical data extracted retrospectively from electronic medical records. The pharmacovigilance component utilized reports submitted to the FAERS database from Q1 2004 through Q2 2025. All case details were de-identified prior to analysis.

d46d29bb-edf2-4e8d-a1bb-10770482e429.paper_title: Thrombocytopenia and anemia associated with piperacillin-tazobactam: integrating clinical case series with FAERS disproportionality analysis
d46d29bb-edf2-4e8d-a1bb-10770482e429.text: The data for this study were sourced from adverse event reports in the FAERS database, covering Q1 2004 to Q2 2025. FAERS is an open-access database that tracks the safety profiles of drugs on the market. The FAERS database contains 7 structured datasets: DEMO (demographic characteristics), DRUG (drug exposure information), REAC (adverse reaction details), OUTC (clinical outcome), RPSR (report source), THER (duration of drug therapy), and INDI (treatment indication information). The FAERS data used in this study were collected, cleaned, and preprocessed using SAS software (version 9.4, SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA). This process included encoding and classifying the preferred terms (PTs) and Standardized MedDRA Queries (SMQs), which were recorded in the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA, version 28.0).

c0fc344c-22f8-4410-9f4b-77f88c185bae.text: Substantial evidence underscores the strong association between metabolic dysfunction-associated Steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and T2DM, as both conditions share insulin resistance as a core pathophysiological mechanism and often co-occur ( 7 ). As the central organ of energy metabolism, the liver, when affected by excessive fat deposition, not only exhibits the hallmark of MASLD but also acts as a key driver of systemic insulin resistance and glucose metabolic dysregulation ( 8 , 9 ). Therefore, precise quantification of liver fat content in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism represents a promising critical biomarker indicating underlying diabetes risk, facilitating more accurate risk stratification ( 10 ).

6afce6c9-e903-4441-b02e-a2425f9eefa9.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
6afce6c9-e903-4441-b02e-a2425f9eefa9.text:
Substantial evidence underscores the strong association between metabolic dysfunction-associated Steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and T2DM, as both conditions share insulin resistance as a core pathophysiological mechanism and often co-occur ( 7 ). As the central organ of energy metabolism, the liver, when affected by excessive fat deposition, not only exhibits the hallmark of MASLD but also acts as a key driver of systemic insulin resistance and glucose metabolic dysregulation ( 8 , 9 ). Therefore, precise quantification of liver fat content in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism represents a promising critical biomarker indicating underlying diabetes risk, facilitating more accurate risk stratification ( 10 ).

Therefore, this study aims to establish a precise dose-response relationship between hepatic steatosis quantified by MRI-PDFF and the prevalence of T2DM in a cross-sectional cohort of postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism.

In addition, we seek to evaluate the potential mediating role of liver enzymes and to explore the nonlinear relationship between liver fat fraction and insulin resistance in this specific population. Elucidating these relationships has the potential to facilitate precise risk stratification within this cohort and to offer a robust evidence base for implementing early interventions for high-risk individuals.

f08c4484-0202-4d06-9e6e-7918838aeb9d.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
f08c4484-0202-4d06-9e6e-7918838aeb9d.heading_path: Materials and methods > Study design and participants
f08c4484-0202-4d06-9e6e-7918838aeb9d.text:
This study was conducted from April 2024 to November 2025 and was approved by the Ethics Committee. The inclusion criteria were as follows: female patients aged 50–80 years who underwent health examinations at our institution and required both liver PDFF assessment and biochemical testing. The exclusion criteria were as follows: acute liver injury, drug-induced chronic liver disease, pre-menopausal female patients, severe cardiovascular disease, obesity secondary to other causes, hepatic or renal dysfunction, autoimmune diseases, active infectious diseases, history of malignant tumors, history of paralysis, as well as current smokers or individuals consuming alcohol.

The diagnosis of prediabetes and diabetes was based on the 2021 American Diabetes Association criteria. Prediabetes was defined as a hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) level of 5.7–6.4% ( 19 ). After applying the detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria, 96 patients were enrolled in the final study cohort, comprising 50 diagnosed with T2DM and 46 with prediabetes.

85c68f96-6c22-4876-87d8-3b52d7fad19c.heading_path: Materials and methods > QCT examinations and image analysis
85c68f96-6c22-4876-87d8-3b52d7fad19c.text: QCT scans and image analysis were performed for all participants. Abdominal CT scans were acquired using an asynchronous quantitative CT protocol on a 128-slice multidetector CT scanner (Somatom Sensation, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany). Participants were positioned supine, with their arms raised above their heads. The scanning range extended from the inferior margin of the 12th thoracic vertebra to the superior margin of the 4th lumbar vertebra. Details of the acquisition parameters are as follows: tube voltage 120 kV, tube current 125 mAs, pixel size 0.78 mm, pitch 0.8, matrix 512 × 512, field of view 500 mm, and slice thickness 1 mm. The images were transferred to a dedicated QCT workstation and analyzed using the body composition analysis module (Mindways Software Inc., Austin, TX, USA; Version 5.10). Visceral fat mass at the level of the L3 vertebral body(L3-VFM) was measured semi-automatically with manual adjustments where necessary. This measurement was based on reconstructed images with a slice thickness of 1 mm. Visceral fat mass was quantified by two independent observers blinded to the participants’ clinical characteristics and diagnostic status, ensuring objectivity of the measurements.

126dbd44-4ceb-446f-91e0-5468ae0229e5.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
126dbd44-4ceb-446f-91e0-5468ae0229e5.heading_path: Materials and methods > Clinical data collection and laboratory examinations
126dbd44-4ceb-446f-91e0-5468ae0229e5.text: Following an overnight fast of at least 8 hours, venous blood samples were collected from the antecubital vein of all participants the next morning for biochemical analysis. The measured parameters included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), AST/ALT ratio, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG, mmol/L), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), very low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (VLDL-C), fasting plasma glucose (FPG, mmol/L), urea, creatinine (Cr), uric acid (UA), calcium (Ca), phosphorus (P), magnesium (Mg), and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). In addition, general clinical information, including age, sex, and body mass index (BMI), was collected. Following biochemical analysis, the TyG index was calculated using the following formula: TyG = ln [Fasting Triglycerides (mg/dL) × Fasting Plasma Glucose (mg/dL)/2].

37170704-673a-4acf-bfd4-90f638e5a7f2.text: R software (version 4.2.2), along with MSTATA software ( www.mstata.com ) were used for statistical analysis. GraphPad Prism (v10.1.2, GraphPad Software, San Diego, California, USA, www.graphpad.com ) was used for drawing figures. Normality of continuous variables was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Data are presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) or median (interquartile range, IQR), for normally and non-normally distributed variables, respectively. Group comparisons were performed using independent samples t-tests for parametric data and Mann-Whitney U tests for non-parametric data, as appropriate. 5c6d7819-212e-4194-bb3e-a55101da2186.text: Inter-observer agreement for hepatic fat fraction, pancreatic fat fraction, and visceral fat mass assessed by two independent blinded observers was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman plots, where an ICC value greater than 0.75 was considered indicative of good reproducibility.

0d2290b7-d291-4168-a352-12999710bbfe.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
0d2290b7-d291-4168-a352-12999710bbfe.heading_path: Materials and methods > Multivariable logistic regression
0d2290b7-d291-4168-a352-12999710bbfe.text: The association between FF-LL levels and T2DM was assessed using multivariable logistic regression. FF-LL was analyzed in two ways: first as a continuous variable, and second categorized into quartiles (Q1–Q4, with Q1 as the reference group) to evaluate a potential dose-response relationship. Covariate selection was guided by prior literature and biological plausibility. To isolate the independent contribution of liver fat deposition to diabetes prevalence in this high-risk population, a sequential adjustment approach was employed. To progressively isolate the unique contribution of liver fat deposition to diabetes prevalence in this high-risk population, a sequential adjustment strategy was employed. Model 1 included age and BMI to account for the physiological decline in β-cell function and insulin sensitivity with advancing age, as well as the confounding effect of overall obesity. Model 2 further adjusted for TC to control for potential confounding by dyslipidemia—a common comorbidity strongly associated with insulin resistance. In Model 3, visceral fat mass was additionally incorporated to evaluate whether the association between liver fat and T2DM was independent of visceral adiposity, given that BMI does not accurately reflect fat distribution. This stepwise adjustment approach was designed to progressively isolate the independent contribution of liver fat deposition.

4301e054-42c4-4e96-a6c5-b3a7e995d2c7.text: To further investigate the utility of FF-LL as a risk stratification biomarker for T2DM in postmenopausal women, we evaluated its discriminative ability by calculating the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

108c02c0-01dc-4138-9e2f-e0c17f603247.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
108c02c0-01dc-4138-9e2f-e0c17f603247.text: To investigate the potential mediating role of liver enzymes, a mediation analysis was performed within the association between FF-LL and T2DM. In this analysis, FF-LL was treated as the exposure, T2DM as the outcome, and liver enzyme levels as the putative mediators. This analysis quantified both the direct effect of FF-LL on T2DM and its indirect effect mediated through liver enzymes.

6ac77910-5bd9-4c47-b8f3-e5bb88b8d80d.text: To further explore the potential nonlinear relationship between liver fat and insulin resistance, the association between FF-LL and the TyG index was assessed using restricted cubic splines.

df2904d8-ef32-4be8-bac3-280b804c78b6.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
df2904d8-ef32-4be8-bac3-280b804c78b6.text:
After screening according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria, a total of 96 postmenopausal women were finally enrolled, including 46 patients with prediabetes and 50 patients with T2DM. The baseline characteristics of the patients were summarized in Table 1 . Overall, compared to the prediabetes group, patients with T2DM demonstrated a more unfavorable metabolic profile, exhibiting higher levels of lipid parameters (TC, HDL-C, LDL-C), liver injury markers (AST/ALT), as well as increased fasting blood glucose, FPG, HbA1c and TyG index.

Regarding the hepatic fat fraction (FF), which was the focus of this study, patients with T2DM showed a significantly higher FF in the left hepatic lobe (FF-LL) compared to the prediabetes group [5.4 (2.8, 8.0) vs. 2.7 (2.2, 5.0); P = 0.015]. The FF in the right anterior lobe, right posterior lobe, and the whole liver also appeared higher in the T2DM group, although these differences did not reach statistical significance. There were no significant differences in the pancreatic fat fraction or L3-VFM between the two groups ( Figure 2 ).

b641196a-c0cb-4c2b-8b0d-f88029e48344.text: Excellent agreement was exhibited across all liver measurements and VFM. Specifically, Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) values indicated excellent reliability: 0.977 (95% CI: 0.965–0.985) for FF-LL, 0.983 (95% CI: 0.974–0.988) for fat fraction of the Right Anterior Lobe, 0.981 (95% CI: 0.971–0.987) for fat fraction of the Right Posterior Lobe, and 0.984 (95% CI: 0.976–0.990) for VFM. Bland-Altman plots revealed that differences between observers were distributed symmetrically around the mean difference, with no systematic bias ( Figure 3 ). In contrast, pancreatic measurements showed moderate agreement, with ICC values ranging from 0.602 to 0.637. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that liver measurements and VFM are highly reproducible and reliable across independent observers.

2df501ed-5b06-46ae-984a-88967373240e.paper_title: A dose-response study of the association between MRI-derived liver proton density fat fraction and prevalent T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism
2df501ed-5b06-46ae-984a-88967373240e.heading_path: Results > Association between left lobe hepatic fat fraction and T2DM risk
2df501ed-5b06-46ae-984a-88967373240e.text: Logistic regression analyses showed that LL-FF is an independent risk factor for T2DM in postmenopausal women with abnormal glucose metabolism, and its effect remains stable after adjusting for age, BMI, TC, and VFM. As shown in Table 2 , when analyzed as a continuous variable, FF-LL was significantly associated with higher prevalence of T2DM across all adjusted models. In the adjusted model with additional adjustment for age and BMI (Model 1), each unit increase in FF-LL was associated with a 15% higher prevalence of T2DM (OR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.02–1.31, P = 0.025). This association strengthened with further adjustment for TC in Model 2 (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.05–1.38, P = 0.01) and remained significant after additional adjustment for L3-VFM in Model 3 (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03–1.34, P = 0.013). This indicates that after adjusting for different sets of covariates, each unit increase in FF-LL was associated with a 15% to 20% increase in the prevalence of T2DM.
